name: MHC class II deficiency (bare lymphocyte syndrome type II)

reference.source: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders / IUIS classification of inborn errors of immunity
clinicalPearls: Presents in infancy or early childhood with a combined immunodeficiency, recurrent respiratory and gastrointestinal infection, chronic diarrhoea and failure to thrive
The defining feature is absent HLA class II (HLA-DR, DP, DQ) expression on antigen-presenting cells and other cells, demonstrated by flow cytometry
It is not caused by defects in the HLA genes themselves but by mutations in the transcription factors that regulate their expression, principally CIITA, RFX5, RFXAP and RFXANK
Because positive selection of CD4 cells depends on class II, there is marked CD4 T-cell lymphopenia with a reduced CD4:CD8 ratio, while CD8 numbers are relatively preserved
Antibody responses are impaired owing to defective CD4-dependent T-cell help despite normal B-cell numbers, producing hypogammaglobulinaemia
Sclerosing cholangitis, often linked to chronic Cryptosporidium infection, and other opportunistic infections are important complications
Inheritance is autosomal recessive and is more prevalent in populations with high consanguinity, notably of North African origin
Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the only curative treatment but outcomes are less favourable than in some other combined immunodeficiencies
reference.pathophysiology: MHC class II deficiency results from loss-of-function variants in the transcriptional regulators that drive HLA class II gene expression, most often CIITA, RFX5, RFXAP or RFXANK, rather than from defects in the HLA loci themselves. Without these regulators, class II molecules are not expressed on antigen-presenting cells, so peptides cannot be presented to CD4 T cells; positive selection of CD4 thymocytes fails, causing profound CD4 lymphopenia, and mature CD4 cells cannot be activated. The lack of effective CD4 help cripples antibody production and cell-mediated immunity, yielding a combined immunodeficiency with susceptibility to a broad range of viral, bacterial, fungal and protozoal pathogens.
additionalDifferentials: Severe combined immunodeficiency of other genotype
MHC class I deficiency (bare lymphocyte syndrome type I)
CD4 lymphopenia from other T-cell defects
additionalInvestigations: Flow cytometry for HLA class II (HLA-DR) expression on monocytes and B cells
Lymphocyte subsets showing CD4 lymphopenia and a reduced CD4:CD8 ratio
Serum immunoglobulins and specific antibody responses
Sequencing of CIITA, RFX5, RFXAP and RFXANK
Investigation for opportunistic infection including Cryptosporidium and hepatobiliary imaging for sclerosing cholangitis
redFlags: Progressive cholestasis suggesting sclerosing cholangitis with cryptosporidial infection
Opportunistic or disseminated infection in an infant with CD4 lymphopenia
Failure to thrive with chronic intractable diarrhoea
Complications following live vaccination or non-irradiated blood products
reference.prognosis: The natural history is poor with early mortality from infection and hepatobiliary disease; allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation offers the only cure but survival is lower than for several other combined immunodeficiencies, underlining the value of early diagnosis.
pitfalls: Assuming the defect lies in the HLA genes rather than their transcriptional regulators
Overlooking the diagnosis because B-cell numbers and total lymphocyte count can be normal
Not measuring HLA class II expression directly by flow cytometry
Missing cryptosporidial infection and evolving sclerosing cholangitis
Giving live vaccines or non-irradiated blood products before diagnosis
references: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders in Infants and Children
IUIS Expert Committee classification of inborn errors of immunity
management: Offer early allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation as the only curative treatment for this combined immunodeficiency
Give infection prophylaxis with co-trimoxazole against Pneumocystis alongside antifungal and antiviral prophylaxis
Provide immunoglobulin replacement therapy for the associated antibody deficiency
Treat intercurrent and opportunistic infections aggressively, using only irradiated cytomegalovirus-safe blood products and avoiding live vaccines
Prevent Cryptosporidium exposure with boiled or filtered water and undertake hepatobiliary surveillance for sclerosing cholangitis
Provide nutritional support for chronic diarrhoea and failure to thrive through immunology, transplant, and hepatology teams
Offer genetic counselling and family screening for the causative transcription-factor variants (CIITA, RFX5, RFXAP, RFXANK) and HLA-type siblings as potential donors
